mechanics.mana_system: No mana system - cards have levels/ranks and summoning conditions
mechanics.color_system: Attributes: DARK, LIGHT, EARTH, WATER, FIRE, WIND, DIVINE
mechanics.special_rules: Going first advantage (55-60% win rate). Hand traps (9-15 in modern decks). Starter vs Extender theory. One-card combos. No mana means any card can be played immediately if summoning conditions are met.

terminology.Hand Trap: Monster activated from hand during opponent's turn to disrupt. NOT all hand traps are interchangeable -- each stops different things (searches vs effects vs summons)
terminology.Starter: Card that initiates combo without needing other cards. 11-13 copies for 82-91% opening consistency
terminology.Extender: Card that provides additional resources mid-combo. Useless without a starter
terminology.Floodgate: Continuous effect restricting opponent (e.g., Skill Drain, Rivalry of Warlords). Often banned/limited
terminology.Board Breaker: Card designed to break established boards when going second (Dark Ruler No More, Lightning Storm, Evenly Matched). Dead or weak going first
terminology.Engine: Self-contained multi-card combo package. Can be archetype-native or splashed into other decks
terminology.Splashable Engine: Small (6-8 card) engine package from one archetype that gets added into unrelated decks for value
terminology.Garnet: A card you must run for an engine to work but never want to draw (named after Gem-Knight Garnet)
terminology.Generic Card: Card usable in any deck regardless of archetype (hand traps, staple spells)
terminology.Archetype-Specific: Card that only functions within its named archetype due to name-based support conditions
terminology.Going First Package: Cards optimized for establishing a board (combo pieces, negates). Different from going-second package
terminology.Going Second Package: Cards optimized for breaking opponent's board (board breakers, hand traps). Different from going-first package

critical_distinctions: Two cards with similar effects from DIFFERENT archetypes are NOT interchangeable if one is archetype-specific (references archetype name in text)
Hand traps are NOT all similar -- Ash Blossom stops searches, Nibiru punishes 5+ summons, Impermanence negates on-field effects. Different functions, different meta calls
Going-first cards and going-second cards serve different purposes even if both are 'disruption'
Engine cards only function with their supporting pieces -- a Snake-Eye searcher is not similar to a generic searcher like ROTA
Banlist status is a hard gate -- a Forbidden card and its closest legal alternative are the key 'similarity pair' for players

card_categories_for_similarity.standalone_generics: Cards in any deck without support: Ash Blossom, Infinite Impermanence, Pot of Prosperity
card_categories_for_similarity.engine_cards: Cards requiring archetype support to function: archetype-specific searchers, extenders, payoffs
card_categories_for_similarity.splashable_engines: Small packages added to unrelated decks: Snake-Eye engine, Tenpai engine
card_categories_for_similarity.tech_cards: Meta-dependent slots targeting specific matchups or strategies

hand_trap_taxonomy.search_negation: Ash Blossom & Joyous Spring -- stops add-from-deck, summon-from-deck, send-from-deck-to-GY
hand_trap_taxonomy.effect_negation: Infinite Impermanence -- negates activated monster effects on field
hand_trap_taxonomy.mass_disruption: Nibiru, the Primal Being -- tributes all after 5th summon, punishes long combo chains
hand_trap_taxonomy.targeted_destruction: Ghost Ogre & Snow Rabbit -- destroys card when it activates an effect on field
hand_trap_taxonomy.draw_punishment: Maxx 'C' -- draws a card for each opponent special summon (where legal)
hand_trap_taxonomy.graveyard_disruption: D.D. Crow, Called by the Grave -- removes GY resources

common_llm_mistakes: Treating all hand traps as similar because they activate from hand -- they stop completely different things
Marking archetype-specific searchers as similar to generic searchers -- they are NOT interchangeable outside the archetype
Ignoring banlist status -- a Forbidden card cannot substitute for anything in competitive play
Conflating going-first and going-second cards as 'both disruption' -- different game states, different functions
Missing archetype name conditions in support card text (e.g., 'target one Snake-Eye card' is NOT generic recursion)

examples.reasoning: Both are Blue-Eyes monsters. Alternative has alternative summoning condition. Similar function in Blue-Eyes decks. Archetype-specific -- neither is useful outside Blue-Eyes.

Both are Level 3 FIRE Spellcaster hand traps that discard to activate. But Ash stops searches/summons-from-deck (80% of combo openers), while Ghost Ogre destroys on-field activated effects (narrower). Different meta functions despite surface similarity. NOT substitutes in most contexts.

Both are staple hand traps in the generic disruption category. Ash negates deck-based effects; Impermanence negates on-field monster effects. Both are going-first and going-second viable. Similar role (generic disruption) but different targets.

Both are disruption, but Dark Ruler No More is a going-second board breaker (dead going first), while Ash Blossom is a hand trap usable in both game states. Different categories despite both being 'disruption'.

Both search a monster from deck. But Snake-Eye Ash is archetype-specific (only functions in Snake-Eye engine), while ROTA is a generic Warrior searcher. Not interchangeable outside Snake-Eye decks despite similar effect text.
